# skill_determinism

Two runs of the same experiment give the same bits — for the same code, the same frozen input window and the same execution environment, never a byte-identical rebuild of that environment at an arbitrary future date: thread caps at one, one fixed seed, pinned orders and a sort before every write, and speed only from processes side by side. *The repository shows the destination, not the road*: bit parity is the proof, and no test suite stands in for it.

## Determinism

- `DETERMINISM-THREAD-CAPS-FROZEN-AT-ONE`
  - Description: Thread caps stay at one on any machine size: a multi-threaded float sum reorders its terms, and two runs diverge.
  - Scope: `**/*.py`, `docker-compose.yml`
  - Expected: `nthread` at one in `XGBOOST_FIXED_PARAMETERS`, `SET threads=1` on every DuckDB connection, `OMP_NUM_THREADS` at one in the environment of the compose anchor every service inherits, and any other library that would thread capped the same way; never raised for a larger machine.
  - Exception: none
- `DETERMINISM-SEED-IS-FIXED-AND-SEARCH-SEQUENTIAL`
  - Description: The seed is fixed and the search runs sequentially: a parallel study draws its trials in an order no second run repeats.
  - Scope: `**/*.py`
  - Expected: One fixed seed, the record `SEED`, in every study's sampler and every fit, and every study optimised with `n_jobs=1`.
  - Exception: none
- `DETERMINISM-AGGREGATIONS-PIN-THEIR-ORDER`
  - Description: An aggregation pins its order and an artifact writer sorts before writing, so the same input writes the same output.
  - Scope: `**/*.py`
  - Expected: An explicit order at every DuckDB aggregation — `arg_min` or `arg_max` by timestamp, an explicit `ORDER BY` — and a sort before every write: the rows of a Parquet file ordered as it is written, `sort_keys` on every JSON a stage writes.
  - Exception: none

## Performance

- `DETERMINISM-SPEED-COMES-FROM-PROCESSES`
  - Description: Speed comes from independent processes side by side, never from raising a thread cap inside one.
  - Scope: `Makefile`, `**/*.py`
  - Expected: One one-off container per asset — the Makefile's `fanout` and the serpentine search's loop — the processes side by side, each under the same `SEED` and the same caps.
  - Exception: none
- `DETERMINISM-WIDTH-IS-ONE-UNLESS-A-HAND-WIDENS-A-RUN`
  - Description: The fan-out runs one asset at a time unless a hand widens one run on the make line; no width is measured or written for a machine, and the hand that widens a run answers for the memory of `JOBS` containers side by side.
  - Scope: `Makefile`
  - Expected: `JOBS ?= 1` in the `Makefile`, the width of every per-asset stage and of the serpentine search's loop; `JOBS=<n>` on the make line widening that run alone; no formula, no measurement and no default written for any machine.
  - Exception: `data-ingest`, one asset at a time whatever `JOBS` says: a memory ceiling is per process, and the sum of the concurrent ceilings is what the host must hold.
- `DETERMINISM-ONE-WRITER-STAYS-SEQUENTIAL`
  - Description: A stage that is the only writer to a shared resource stays sequential.
  - Scope: `Makefile`
  - Expected: That stage run once, in one process, whatever `JOBS` says — each status stage, the one writer of its snapshot, through the Makefile's `basket` over the whole basket.
  - Exception: none
- `DETERMINISM-MEASURE-BEFORE-AND-AFTER`
  - Description: An optimisation is measured before and after against the run-to-run spread, and one inside the spread is noise and is rejected.
  - Scope: `**/*.py`
  - Expected: Records of `store/run_records/` with the same `stage` and `command` on unchanged input, taken before the change and after it, their `duration_seconds` compared; a gain inside their spread rejected.
  - Exception: none
